taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. 

In 2026, the United States transitions from Daylight Saving Time on November 1, so Pacific Time on October 30 will be **PDT (UTC-7)**. Spain transitions from Summer Time (CEST) to Central European Time (CET) on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on the deadline date of October 30, Madrid will be on **CET (UTC+1)**.

Madrid (UTC+1) is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Daylight Time (UTC-7). Adding 8 hours to Friday at 11:59 PM results in Saturday at 7:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. "This coming Monday" refers to Monday, November 2, 2026.

To determine the local time in Madrid, we must account for the end of Daylight Saving Time (DST) in both regions:
1. **Madrid, Spain**: Europe ends DST on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this occurs on October 25. Thus, on Monday, November 2, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.
2. **Los Angeles, USA**: The United States ends DST on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, this occurs on Sunday, November 1. Thus, on Monday, November 2, Los Angeles will have transitioned to Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is **UTC-8**.

The time difference between PST (UTC-8) and CET (UTC+1) is 9 hours. 
10:00 AM Los Angeles time + 9 hours = 19:00 local time in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon begins on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time. At this time, Spain is observing Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).

During the event, on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 03:00 CEST, the clocks in Madrid will be set back one hour to 02:00 CET (Central European Time, UTC+1) for the end of daylight saving time.

Because the clock moves backward by one hour, the passage of 48 hours in real-time will result in a local end time that is one hour "earlier" than the starting hour:
1. Start: Saturday, Oct 24, 18:00 (UTC+2)
2. After 24 hours: Sunday, Oct 25, 18:00 (UTC+1) — Note that 25 hours of local time have passed due to the clock change.
3. After 48 hours total: Monday, Oct 26, 17:00 (UTC+1)

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest starts on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. Adding exactly 72 hours (3 days) means the submissions close on **October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT**.

To convert this to Madrid local time:
1.  **Daylight Saving Time (DST) Check:** In Europe, DST ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this is Sunday, October 25. Therefore, on October 29, Madrid will be on Central European Time (**CET**), which is **UTC+1**.
2.  **Pacific Time Check:** In North America, DST ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, this is November 1. Therefore, on October 29, the Pacific Time zone is still on Pacific Daylight Time (**PDT**), which is **UTC-7**.
3.  **Calculation:** The difference between UTC-7 and UTC+1 is **8 hours**. Adding 8 hours to 10:00 AM results in 6:00 PM (18:00).

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the local time in Madrid for the announcement, we first establish the submission closing time in UTC. On October 31, 2026, the United States is still on Daylight Saving Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Therefore, 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2026, is 03:59 UTC on November 1, 2026.

The results are announced exactly 36 hours later. Adding 36 hours to November 1, 03:59 UTC gives us:
- 24 hours later: November 2, 03:59 UTC
- 12 additional hours: November 2, 15:59 UTC

Finally, we convert the UTC announcement time to Madrid local time. Spain ends Daylight Saving Time on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). By November 2, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
15:59 UTC + 1 hour = 16:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the local time in Tokyo, Japan (JST, which is UTC+9) for the Unix timestamp 1791788340, we follow these steps:

1.  **Calculate the UTC date and time:**
    *   The timestamp 1791788340 represents the number of seconds elapsed since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC).
    *   Dividing 1791788340 by the number of seconds in a day (86,400) gives approximately 20,738.29097 days since the epoch.
    *   Subtracting the number of days for the 56 years from 1970 to 2026 (including 14 leap years: 1972, 76, 80, 84, 88, 92, 96, 2000, 04, 08, 12, 16, 20, 24) which is $56 \times 365 + 14 = 20,454$ days, leaves 284.29097 days into the year 2026.
    *   The 285th day of 2026 (284 full days completed) is October 12, 2026.
    *   The fractional part of the day ($0.29097 \times 24$ hours) is 06:59:00 UTC.

2.  **Convert UTC to Tokyo Local Time (JST):**
    *   Tokyo is in the Japan Standard Time zone (JST), which is UTC+9.
    *   Adding 9 hours to the UTC time of 06:59:00 on October 12, 2026, gives 15:59:00 on the same day.

3.  **Format the final result:**
    *   Date: 2026-10-12
    *   Time: 15:59

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is provided in UTC (indicated by the "Z"). To convert this to your local time in Madrid, Spain, we need to determine the correct time zone offset for October 25, 2026.

1.  **Time Zone Transition:** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in Spain ends on Sunday, October 25th. At 03:00 CEST (01:00 UTC), the clocks are set back one hour to 02:00 CET.
2.  **Determine the Offset:** The deadline is 02:30 UTC. Since 02:30 UTC occurs after the 01:00 UTC transition, Madrid will have already switched from UTC+2 (CEST) to UTC+1 (CET).
3.  **Calculate Local Time:** 
    *   UTC Time: 02:30
    *   Offset: +1 hour
    *   Local Time: 03:30

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid local time, we first identify the specific date and time in the Pacific Time zone and then apply the necessary conversions.

1.  **Date Identification**: The last Sunday of October 2026 is **October 25, 2026**.
2.  **Pacific Time (PT)**: In the United States, Daylight Saving Time (PDT) ends on the first Sunday of November. Therefore, on October 25, the Pacific Time zone is still using **Pacific Daylight Time (PDT)**, which is **UTC-7**.
3.  **Madrid Time**: In Spain, Daylight Saving Time (CEST) ends on the last Sunday of October. On **October 25, 2026, at 03:00 AM**, clocks in Madrid move back one hour to **Central European Time (CET)**, which is **UTC+1**.
4.  **Time Conversion**: The deadline is 11:59 PM (23:59) PDT on October 25. Since Madrid is at UTC+1 and Pacific Time is at UTC-7, Madrid is **8 hours ahead** of Pacific Time at that specific moment.
    *   23:59 (Oct 25) + 8 hours = 07:59 (Oct 26).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the United States ends daylight saving time on Sunday, November 1. At 2:00 AM on that day, clocks roll back to Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5. Lima, Peru, remains on Peru Time (PET) year-round, which is also UTC-5. Therefore, 12:00 noon Eastern Time on that day will be exactly 12:00 noon in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is a time zone equivalent to UTC-12. Tokyo, Japan (JST) is in the UTC+9 time zone. 

To convert from AoE to Tokyo local time, you calculate the time difference:
9 (JST) - (-12 (AoE)) = 21 hours.

This means Tokyo is 21 hours ahead of AoE. The deadline of "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is the same as "January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE." Adding 21 hours to that time results in 21:00 on January 1, 2027.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 5, 2026, Sydney, Australia, will be on Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), which is UTC+11. On that same day, New York, USA, will be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. 

To convert Sydney time to New York time:
1.  Sydney is 11 hours ahead of UTC (17:00 - 11 hours = 06:00 UTC).
2.  New York is 4 hours behind UTC (06:00 UTC - 4 hours = 02:00 New York time).
3.  The time difference between Sydney and New York is 15 hours.
4.  Subtracting 15 hours from 17:00 (5:00 PM) on October 5 results in 02:00 (2:00 AM) on the same day, October 5.

Since you are in New York that week and require the deadline in New York time, the calculation is as follows:

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
